THE HOLONOMY BRAIDING FOR Uξ(sl2) IN TERMS OF GEOMETRIC
QUANTUM DILOGARITHMS
CALVIN MCPHAIL-SNYDER AND NICOLAI RESHETIKHIN
Abstract. We derive an explicit formula for the holonomy R-matrix of quantum sl2 at a
root of unity. We show it factorizes into a product of four quantum dilogarithms and satisfies
a holonomy Yang-Baxter equation. This factorization extends previously known results and
we collect many existing results needed for our computation.

[]{#sec:Introduction label="sec:Introduction"}

Holonomy $R$-matrices were used in [@Kashaev2005] to describe invariants of knots with flat connections in the complement. These $R$-matrices were introduced in [@Reshetikhin1995] to describe the braiding for the de Concini-Kac specialization of quantum groups corresponding to simple finite dimensional Lie algebras at a root of unity. In that case the quantized universal enveloping algebra is finite dimensional over the central Hopf subalgebra. blocks.title: Representation into the Weyl algebra
blocks.content:
The $q$-Weyl algebra $W_q$ is an associative algebra over $\mathbb{C}[q, q^{-1}]$ generated by invertible generators $x,y$ satisfying $$xy = q^2 yx.$$ The following is well known:

::: proposition
There is a unique algebra homomorphism $\phi : \mathcal{U}_q(\sla) \to W_q[z,z^{-1}]$ acting on generators as $$\phi(K)=x, \ \ \phi(E)=qy(z-x), \ \ \phi(F)=y^{-1}(1-z^{-1}x^{-1})$$
:::

It is easy to compute the image of the Casimir: $$\phi(\Omega) = qz + (qz)^{-1}.$$ From now on we write $\mathcal{W}_q = W_q[z, z^{-1}]$.

blocks.title: Uξ-modules.
blocks.content:
We say a $\mathcal{U}_\xi$ module $V$ has character $\chi \in \slg^*$ if $$z \cdot v = \chi(z) v \text{ for all } v \in V, z \in \mathcal{Z}_0.$$ In particular any simple $\mathcal{U}_\xi$-module has a character. Because the multiplication on characters is compatible with the coproduct the category of $\mathcal{U}_\xi$-modules with characters is graded by $\slg^*$: if $V_1, V_2$ have characters $\chi_1, \chi_2$, then $V_1 \otimes V_2$ has character $\chi_1 \cdot \chi_2$.

We now consider the presentation of $\mathcal{U}_q$ in terms of $\mathcal{W}_q$ at $q = \xi$. The map $\phi$ takes the center of $\mathcal{U}_\xi$ to the center of $\mathcal{W}_\xi$:

::: lemma
The center of $\mathcal{W}_{\xi}$ is generated by $z$, $x^N$, and $y^N$ and $\phi$ takes the center of $\mathcal{U}_\xi$ to the center of $\mathcal{W}_{\xi}$. Explicitly, $$\begin{aligned}
      \phi(K^N)
      &=
      x^N
      \\
      \phi(E^N)
      &=
      y^N(x^N - z^N)
      \\
      \phi(F^N)
      &=
      y^{-N}(1 - z^{-N} x^{-N})
    \end{aligned}$$
:::

[]{#sec:braid groupoids label="sec:braid groupoids"}

Next we show our $R$-matrices satisfy braid relations. We discuss how to use these braid relations to define tangle and link invariants in [@McPhailSnyderVolume], extending [@Kashaev2005]. The holonomy $R$-matrix satisfies a *family* of braid relations parametrized by all admissible choices of colors, which have a natural interpretation in terms of flat $\sla$ connections on the braid complement, equivalently representations of the fundamental group of the complement into $\slg$.
